summary: Function template that converts an integral value to a decimal string using the type-erased visitor pattern. Specialised per-T via SFINAE on std::is_integral_v<T>; emits ASCII digits into a fixed-size buffer member, then returns a string_view bounded by the high-water mark. Exception-safe in the strong sense — failure modes are documented by the noexcept signature.

inputs.name: value
inputs.semantic: Integer to format. For all T satisfying std::is_integral_v<T>; INT64_MIN is handled defensively (see EC-1).

outputs.name: result
outputs.semantic: View into the internal buffer; valid for the lifetime of the format_int instance (Borrowed; see OL-1).

invariants.claim: For all integral T, the produced digit sequence equals the decimal expansion of value, with a leading '-' iff value < 0.
The returned string_view's data() always points into the format_int instance's internal buffer — never to a temporary or stack-local.
Output digit count equals floor(log10(|value|)) + 1 for value != 0; 1 for value == 0.

template_instantiations.constraint: requires std::is_integral_v<T> (SFINAE via std::enable_if_t in pre-C++20 fmt)

object_lifetimes.subject: return value (string_view)
object_lifetimes.policy: Caller must not outlive the format_int instance — the string_view aliases the buffer member. The translation target should either copy the data into an owned String at the call site, or keep the format_int alive for the view's duration.

exception_contracts.contract: Marked noexcept. The implementation cannot throw — buffer is fixed-size, no allocations occur on the hot path. C# translation: keep nothrowable. Java translation: declare no `throws` clause.

undefined_behaviors.trigger: value == std::numeric_limits<int_type>::min() AND the implementation negates value to compute its absolute value.

side_effects.description: Writes ASCII digits into format_int::buffer_ — a member array. No I/O; no allocations.

edge_cases.description: INT_MIN (and INT64_MIN for 64-bit T). Naive |value| overflows; the implementation special-cases via unsigned arithmetic.
edge_cases.behavior: Treats |value| as unsigned with the sign bit set; emits the correct decimal expansion.

edge_cases.description: value == 0. Output is single character '0' (not empty).
edge_cases.behavior: INV-3 covers this; explicit branch in the implementation.

open_questions.question: For Java target: should the equivalent return a primitive char[] view (no equivalent of string_view) or a defensive String copy? The Borrowed lifetime model doesn't translate cleanly to Java; either choice changes the allocation profile of callers.
